mostWorthwhile.text: Making the deadwood refuge was most worthwhile: it connected fungi, stored energy and shelter to survival when sunlight-dependent food webs faltered.

leastWorthwhile.text: Trying the small mammals against the forest twice was frustrating; their earlier association with fallen wood seemed relevant, but they had no available operation until the refuge existed.

surprise.text: The mammals cached seeds, some of which could grow later. Their unintended contribution made recovery feel like an ecological relationship rather than a simple reset.

arbitrary.text: The failed attempts with the mammals felt opaque at first: the feedback said they could not combine with anything, without explaining that the refuge had to be created first.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: the decomposer-supported refuge and the seed cache made me curious about how the recovering world might develop, while acknowledging what was lost.
